title: Why the shop runs with so much in it
target: How a full Supermarket Simulator shop is drawn and how placements behave, so a shop that stutters or will not line up can be reasoned about.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop with a lot of stock in it

steps.do: Know that the game decides what you cannot see.
steps.because: the game runs an occlusion controller of its own and records what may be hidden as occludee data (OcclusionController, OccludeeData)

steps.do: Do not count repeated goods as separate objects.
steps.because: repeated objects are held as instance data, with bounds for an instance (InstanceData, InstanceBoundsData)

steps.do: Know that their positions are generated rather than placed by hand.
steps.because: an indexed static instancer generates the matrices the repeated pieces are placed from (IndexedStaticInstancerMatrixGenerator)

steps.do: Expect the walkable floor to be managed separately from the shop.
steps.because: obstacles that people walk around have a manager of their own (NavMeshObstacleManager)

steps.do: Place things in the placement mode rather than by dragging anywhere.
steps.because: placement is a mode, and the modes are held by a manager (IPlacingMode, LayoutModeManager)

steps.do: Expect a placement to be checked before it is accepted.
steps.because: a position validator checks a placement (PositionValidator)

steps.do: Line fixtures up on the grid instead of trusting the eye.
steps.because: a grid of its own is what a placement lines up on (GridManager)

steps.do: Remember that a placement keeps track of its neighbours.
steps.because: a placement records the neighbouring positions it relates to (PlacementNeighbourData)

commonMistakes: Blaming the goods for a stutter when the game is hiding what you cannot see.
Nudging a fixture by eye instead of using the grid.
Assuming a placement that looks wrong was accepted.
Moving one shelf and expecting the fixture beside it not to care.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
